title: Fold an open button-lock pocket knife shut without a gripper ever in the blade's path
instruction: Fold the pocket knife shut, keeping the grippers off its edge, and leave it on the table.
context: Folding a pocket knife shut after opening a parcel or cutting cord is an everyday job in many homes: about 36 million US households own an outdoor or pocket knife (Mediamark, 2008), and pocket/utility knives lead knife injuries treated in US emergency rooms (NEISS 1990-2008). A button lock keeps the blade open until its button is held in, and the closing blade swings its edge through an arc. Unlike retracting a box cutter's blade (TK-V7P9X9), a lock is held while the edge sweeps an arc.
setup: Station table. Coordinates: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, from the midpoint between the bases; table top 0 mm. One button-lock folding knife modelled on the Civivi Button Lock Elementum II (75 mm blade, 104 mm closed), lying flat, button scale up, blade open in line with the handle (180 degrees from shut). Handle: 104 x 30 x 13 mm, two 2 mm olive scales (G10) round a 9 mm channel, a 3 mm dark back spacer along its spine side for the 70 mm nearest the butt, a silver pivot screw head over the pivot, 14 mm from the handle's front end. Blade: steel, 3 mm thick, 24 mm wide, 75 mm out of the handle (89 mm from the pivot), its flat grey and a bright 9 mm edge bevel; the last 8 mm narrows to the point in three square steps, 20, 14 and 8 mm wide. It sits mid-channel, 5 to 8 mm above the table. Lock button: gold, 8 mm across, 20 mm behind the pivot on the upper scale, 1.8 mm proud. Mass 88 g (handle 50 g, blade 30 g, button 8 g). Lot A (screenshot): pivot at x 300, y 0 mm; handle to the robot's right, blade to its left, edge facing away from the robot. Lot B: the same pivot, the knife turned half round: handle to the left, blade to the right, edge facing the robot. Lot C: pivot at x 310, y 0 mm, turned a quarter turn from lot A: handle away from the robot, blade pointing at it, edge facing the robot's left. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, 1.0 if all hold at the end: the blade is within 5 degrees of fully shut (its back at most 4 mm proud of the handle's open side; at 5 degrees every point of the edge is already inside the handle's outline seen from above, at least 3 mm in from its open side, and the detent pulls the blade fully shut from 15 degrees); the knife lies flat on the table (lowest point within 1 mm of it, tilted at most 10 degrees); both grippers are more than 5 mm from the knife; and the knife has been still like this, let go, for 1 s. Otherwise 0. The trial also scores 0 if a gripper touches the cutting edge at any moment: before each trial the outer 3 mm of the edge, both sides, and the tip are coated with engineer's blue marking paste and the finger pads covered white, and any blue mark on a gripper or pad cover afterwards counts. Because the edge leads as the blade closes, this also catches a gripper left in the blade's path. A knife left partly open still has its edge out and gets no credit. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Use the blunted rig knife: the same model with its whole edge ground to a 1 mm flat and its point rounded to 2 mm radius; lock, pivot and blade outline unchanged. Fit both grippers' finger pads with fresh white covers (0.5 mm polyurethane tape). 2. Coat the outer 3 mm of the edge, both sides, and the tip with a thin film of engineer's blue (Prussian blue) marking paste, fresh before every trial. 3. Fold the blade fully open until the lock button pops out and the blade will not fold without pressing it. Lay the knife flat, button scale up. 4. Lot A: pivot screw at x 300, y 0 mm, handle along y to the robot's right, blade to the left, edge facing away. Lot B: same pivot, handle to the left, blade to the right, edge facing the robot. Lot C: pivot screw at x 310, y 0 mm, handle pointing away from the robot, blade pointing at it, edge facing the robot's left. 5. Move both arms to their start pose, clear of the knife. After the trial, check the grippers and pad covers for blue marks; replace marked covers and wipe and re-coat the edge.
fidelity: Rigid parts at the knife's true size and mass; the tip tapers in three square steps. The lock is a rule: the blade cannot leave its open stop unless the button is in 1.2 mm or more. The button takes about 4 N. Channel gap 3 mm above and below the blade. Real trials use a blunted copy (edge ground to a 1 mm flat) and white pad covers. The simulator also zeroes a trial if the closing blade's edge half passes through a gripper between control steps. Three lots stop a fixed habit.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in each of lots A, B and C (each ran the full 40 s); demo: 1.0 in each lot
